content.value_statement: Large object arrays are expensive to process through repeated natural-language instructions. This skill applies reusable JavaScript transformations and returns compact processing statistics.
actual_capabilities: Filters object arrays with a caller-provided predicate.
Maps records through a caller-provided transformation function.
Sorts records by one field in ascending or descending order.
Calculates sum, average, count, minimum, or maximum for one field.
Removes duplicate field values and reports input, output, and operation statistics.
limitations: The supplied implementation accepts arrays only and expects object-like records.
Grouping and dataset merging are described but are not implemented in the provided function.
Average on an empty value set returns NaN, and mixed field types can produce unreliable results.
Persistence, database access, and MCP calls require separate tools with appropriate permissions.

use_cases.title: Prepare Analysis Records
use_cases.description: Clean, filter, deduplicate, and sort object arrays before analysis.

use_cases.title: Summarize Operational Data
use_cases.description: Calculate totals, averages, counts, minimums, and maximums for routine reporting.

use_cases.title: Build MCP Data Pipelines
use_cases.description: Transform data returned by an authorized MCP tool before saving or summarizing results.

prompt_templates.title: Filter and Sort Records
prompt_templates.prompt: Process [dataset]. Keep records where [condition], sort by [field] in [ascending or descending] order, and report removed and remaining counts.

prompt_templates.title: Normalize and Deduplicate
prompt_templates.prompt: Normalize [fields] in [dataset], remove duplicates using [unique field], and return the cleaned records with operation statistics.

prompt_templates.title: Transform and Aggregate
prompt_templates.prompt: Transform [dataset] using [mapping rules], filter by [condition], then calculate [sum, average, count, minimum, or maximum] for [field].

prompt_templates.title: Process an MCP Result
prompt_templates.prompt: Use authorized [MCP source] data, apply [transformations], save only to [approved destination], and return statistics instead of the full dataset.

output_examples.input: Keep completed sales, sort by amount from highest to lowest, and summarize the operation.
output: The remaining amounts are ordered from 225 to 150.

output_examples.input: Calculate the total for three order values: 100, 150, and 200.
output_examples.output: The total order value is 450 across three records.

output_examples.input: Normalize customer names and emails, then remove duplicate emails.
output_examples.output: Two unique customer records remain after trimming names, lowercasing emails, and removing one duplicate.

best_practices: Validate array shape, field names, and value types before processing.
Save intermediate results when large transformations need recovery or inspection.
Return concise statistics when the full processed dataset is unnecessary.
anti_patterns: Do not assume grouping or merging is available in the supplied implementation.
Do not pass unreviewed transformation callbacks from untrusted sources.
Do not use database or storage tools without explicit authorization and destination checks.

faq.question: Which input format does this skill accept?
faq.answer: The provided function accepts a JavaScript array, usually containing object records.

faq.question: Which aggregation operations are supported?
faq.answer: It supports sum, average, count, minimum, and maximum for one selected field.

faq.question: Can it group or merge datasets?
faq.answer: The documentation mentions both features, but the supplied implementation does not include them.

faq.question: Does it access databases or storage automatically?
faq.answer: No. Database and storage access require separate authorized MCP tools.

faq.question: Does it modify the original array?
faq.answer: It copies the outer array before processing, but callback functions can still mutate record objects.

faq.question: How should empty or mixed-type data be handled?
faq.answer: Validate values first because empty averages return NaN and mixed types can affect sorting or arithmetic.
